title: HM Land Registry OKF candidate personas and user stories
description: Task-based hypotheses for evaluating discovery of HM Land Registry public information. These are not demographic profiles and are not claims that user research has validated the roles.

evidence_policy.rule: A persona is included only where an official source exposes a corresponding task, service, data product, access route or assurance need.
prohibitions: Do not invent age, gender, ethnicity, disability, income, location or technical skill.
Do not treat a professional label as evidence that every member of that profession has the same need.
Do not promote a candidate persona to validated without cited independent user research.

personas.name: Public property-information user
personas.role_basis: Official GOV.UK guidance exposes public tasks for finding title information, understanding boundaries and searching local land charges.
personas.need: Find the correct official service or guidance, understand what the returned information can establish and recover when an address search is incomplete.
main_risks: Treating an online title copy as official proof of ownership.
Treating a title-plan line as an exact legal boundary.
Using a service outside its England-and-Wales scope.
evidence_of_success: The result identifies the official HMLR or GOV.UK route.
The legal and evidential limitation is visible before the user follows the route.
Alternative official routes such as official copies or a search of the index map are discoverable when applicable.

personas.name: Conveyancing practitioner
personas.role_basis: HMLR publishes practice guides, portal guidance, official-copy procedures and Business Gateway material for professional land-registration work.
personas.need: Resolve the current official guidance, evidential document or professional service route for a defined conveyancing task.
main_risks: Relying on superseded guidance or an unofficial summary.
Missing titles that affect a property when searching only by address.
Confusing general, agreed and determined boundary evidence.
evidence_of_success: The result preserves the guide or service identity and current official URL.
Access, fee and account requirements are visible.
The answer distinguishes procedural guidance from legal advice and source evidence.

personas.name: Lending and valuation evidence user
personas.role_basis: HMLR describes registered charges and lenders in title information and publishes transaction data used in property-market analysis.
personas.need: Distinguish title evidence, registered-charge information, transaction data and derived market indicators before relying on them in lending or valuation work.
main_risks: Treating a historic price-paid value as a current valuation.
Treating catalogue or bundle dates as register or dataset currency.
Treating a title summary or bulk dataset as a substitute for the required official evidence.
evidence_of_success: The record states the evidence type, coverage period and source date separately.
The route to official title evidence is distinguishable from analytical datasets.
Licence and third-party address-data constraints remain visible.

personas.name: Data and GIS practitioner
personas.role_basis: The Use land and property data catalogue publishes tabular and spatial products, formats, update schedules and GIS requirements.
personas.need: Discover a suitable dataset, inspect its schema, spatial meaning, coverage, vintage, delivery format and permitted use before reuse.
main_risks: Presenting indicative polygons as exact legal title boundaries.
Assuming all datasets have the same licence, access model or API.
Claiming complete local-authority or geographic coverage without a dated denominator.
evidence_of_success: Format, CRS or spatial semantics, vintage and source are explicit where available.
The dataset landing page and technical specification are both recoverable.
Coverage and known omissions are stated without inventing geometry.

personas.name: API and data-integration engineer
personas.role_basis: HMLR publishes API v1 documentation, Business Gateway developer material and public API-catalogue records with materially different access models.
personas.need: Identify the operationally authoritative contract, supported access method, authentication boundary, version and refresh behaviour without exposing credentials.
main_risks: Treating catalogue discovery metadata as the operational API contract.
Calling an authenticated or restricted service without authority.
Persisting API keys, certificates or short-lived signed download links.
evidence_of_success: The publisher-operated API or developer documentation is the operational source.
REST, SOAP/WSDL and transactional services are not conflated.
Account, licence, key or certificate requirements are explicit and no credential is stored.

personas.name: Local-authority land and planning user
personas.role_basis: The national Local Land Charges service and its spatial data expose authority-migration, official-search and indicative-location tasks.
personas.need: Determine whether an authority is covered, distinguish search evidence from spatial discovery data and understand the relationship to planning or land-registration information.
main_risks: Assuming every local authority has migrated to the national register.
Treating an INSPIRE polygon as the complete legal charge or title boundary.
Automating a search service whose terms prohibit software-agent searching or monitoring.
evidence_of_success: Migration and coverage limitations are visible.
Official search, personal search and downloadable spatial data remain distinct.
The route does not imply that CON29 or all planning information is included.

personas.name: Provenance and licensing reviewer
personas.role_basis: HMLR data surfaces publish dataset-specific licences, third-party-rights conditions, attribution text and access constraints that cannot be inferred from public availability.
personas.need: Trace every material claim to a canonical source and verify the applicable licence, attribution, access state, derivation and observation date.
main_risks: Applying the Open Government Licence to content governed by a bespoke or third-party licence.
Using a CKAN or catalogue modification date as dataset currency.
Presenting normalised or derived metadata as an official HMLR assertion.
evidence_of_success: Each result exposes source family, canonical URL, observation date and derivation.
Licence and access states are dataset-specific.
Publisher-operated sources outrank discovery catalogues for operational claims.

personas.name: Accessible-service user and evaluator
personas.role_basis: HMLR publishes accessibility statements and an accessible-documents policy describing keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, focus and alternative-format needs.
personas.need: Complete discovery and evidence-inspection tasks with keyboard and assistive-technology-compatible controls and understand known accessibility limitations.
main_risks: A visual-only map, facet or status signal blocking task completion.
Focus becoming obscured or controls lacking accessible names.
A PDF or spatial result having no usable HTML explanation or alternative route.
evidence_of_success: Search, facets, results and source links are keyboard operable with visible focus.
Status and evidence labels are programmatically available and survive 400 percent zoom.
Known source accessibility limitations and alternative-format routes are disclosed.

personas.name: Wales-focused bilingual service user
personas.role_basis: HMLR's Welsh Language Scheme identifies bilingual public services, correspondence, registers, publications and Welsh terminology needs.
personas.need: Find the Welsh or bilingual form of relevant guidance and preserve Welsh labels, language metadata and Wales-specific service context.
main_risks: Assuming an English route means no Welsh service exists.
Dropping language tags or anglicising source-native Welsh labels.
Allowing a screen reader to mispronounce Welsh place names because language changes are unmarked.
evidence_of_success: Welsh routes or availability are visible from the English result.
English and Welsh labels remain distinct but linked.
Language metadata and known pronunciation limitations are inspectable.

stories.title: Orient to HMLR scope and authority
stories.user_story: As a public information user or reviewer, I want to identify what HM Land Registry covers and which source is authoritative so that I do not apply the bundle beyond England and Wales or mistake discovery metadata for official evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The result names HM Land Registry and its England-and-Wales remit.
The canonical GOV.UK organisation route is visible.
The bundle describes itself as discovery and does not replace the source.

stories.title: Choose the right property-information evidence
stories.user_story: As someone investigating a property, I want title summaries, online copies and official copies to be clearly distinguished so that I obtain evidence fit for my purpose.
acceptance_criteria: Register, title summary and title plan are described separately.
Online copies are not represented as proof of ownership.
The official-copy route and applicable access or fee are recoverable.

stories.title: Interpret title and spatial boundaries safely
stories.user_story: As a property or spatial-data user, I want general, determined and indicative boundaries labelled correctly so that map geometry is not mistaken for an exact legal boundary.
acceptance_criteria: General boundaries are never described as exact.
Determined-boundary guidance is linked when relevant.
INSPIRE and other discovery polygons retain their indicative status.

stories.title: Follow an authorised conveyancing route
stories.user_story: As a conveyancing practitioner, I want to find official-copy, index-map and professional-service guidance with access constraints so that I use an authorised current route.
acceptance_criteria: Address-search limitations and the search-of-index-map alternative are visible.
Portal or Business Gateway access is labelled restricted where applicable.
The bundle never attempts the transaction.

stories.title: Separate lending evidence from market data
stories.user_story: As a lending or valuation evidence user, I want registered-charge information, price-paid data and dates kept distinct so that I do not overstate currency or evidential value.
acceptance_criteria: Title evidence and analytical transaction data are separate result types.
Price paid is not described as current value.
Catalogue, observation, release and registration dates have distinct labels.

stories.title: Assess a dataset for technical reuse
stories.user_story: As a data or GIS practitioner, I want to filter datasets by purpose, format, geography and update behaviour so that I can inspect the right technical specification before reuse.
acceptance_criteria: Dataset landing page, technical specification and download or API route are separate.
Format, GIS requirement and geography metadata are searchable.
Source-native Welsh place names and language metadata are retained.

stories.title: Understand Local Land Charges coverage and meaning
stories.user_story: As a local-land user, I want service coverage, authority migration, official-search evidence and spatial discovery data kept distinct so that I do not claim more than the national register contains.
acceptance_criteria: The result states that not every authority has migrated where that remains true.
Official search and downloadable INSPIRE data are different records.
Planning, CON29, title and local-land-charge concepts are not conflated.

stories.title: Integrate through a documented access boundary
stories.user_story: As an integration engineer, I want to distinguish public metadata, authenticated data APIs and professional transaction services so that automation stays within documented authority.
acceptance_criteria: The API base, version and supported dataset list come from publisher documentation.
Account, accepted licence, API key or certificate requirements are explicit.
No credential, signed URL or automated restricted-service call is emitted.

stories.title: Refresh full and change-only data reproducibly
stories.user_story: As a data maintainer, I want complete and change-only releases, their identifiers and observation dates modelled explicitly so that refreshes are reproducible and do not invent currency.
acceptance_criteria: Full and change-only distributions are distinct.
The monthly release rule comes from the dataset technical specification.
A refresh creates a new observed snapshot rather than rewriting old evidence.

stories.title: Verify licence, attribution and third-party rights
stories.user_story: As a reuse reviewer, I want the licence and attribution for each dataset and field layer so that public accessibility is not mistaken for unrestricted reuse.
acceptance_criteria: OCOD and Price Paid Data licence evidence resolves to the relevant publisher page.
Third-party address-data conditions remain visible.
OGL status is not inherited by a dataset with a bespoke licence.

stories.title: Complete discovery accessibly
stories.user_story: As an accessible-service user or evaluator, I want search, filters, evidence and recovery links to work with keyboard and assistive technology so that discovery is not visual-only.
acceptance_criteria: All critical controls have accessible names and keyboard operation.
Focus remains visible and status changes are announced.
Known source limitations and alternative-format routes are documented.

stories.title: Discover Welsh and bilingual services
stories.user_story: As a Wales-focused user, I want Welsh availability and language metadata shown alongside English records so that the bundle does not erase bilingual service obligations or source labels.
acceptance_criteria: The Welsh Language Scheme is discoverable.
Welsh routes and bilingual-register context are explicit.
Welsh labels retain language metadata, including known pronunciation limitations.
